Fix what the output names. Move the tasks it touches to in_progress with UpdateTask while you work and to tested once their tests pass; leave the rest of the board as it is.

Reproduce the failure with a run narrowed to the test the output names, fix it, then run that test again and build its project. The whole sweep runs again as soon as you stop with every task tested, so stopping on a fix you have not run costs another one.

CodeOutline on the failing test's file gives the line each test starts on: Read that test's range rather than the whole file.

What earlier tasks left:
- Starting the job [tested]: New session mode `doc-migration` (src/agent/session/session-manager.ts: added to SessionMode, isPlanning, isFeatureless, STEPS, titleFor → 'Doc migration'). New phase module src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts exporting docMigrationScope(ignored), DOC_MIGRATION_TOOLS, docMigrationKickoff(), docMigrationPrompt(cwd): scope is readable docs/**+README+specs (never source), writable [], askable docs/** — same shape as docsEvaluationScope but, unlike the 'docs' mode, mode-setup.ts never grants it full access, so it stays scoped for its whole life. Wired into mode-setup.ts (new case, uses ctx.withDocs so the docs map/outline precedes judgment, no ctx.withMap), new-session-view.ts (third card on the Maintenance tab, `.migration-fields` form, no linked-files-row, no count badge), chat-view-provider.ts (kickoff dispatch), and the exhaustive mode maps (sessions-tree MODE_LABEL, plan-step RUN_NOUN, session-groups CONVERSATIONS, docs-map wantsDocsMap, effort STEP_EFFORT). The Pruning/Migrating/Verifying stages (covered-section detection, the feature list, draft spec writing, the approval check) are not implemented here — only the session's scope, tools and the prompt's standing ground rules; later tasks extend docMigrationPrompt and docMigrationScope (e.g. adding plan/*.spec.md to writable) rather than re-deriving the wiring. (files: src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts, src/agent/session/session-manager.ts, src/agent/session/mode-setup.ts, src/agent/session/effort.ts, src/agent/docs-map/session-context.ts, src/chat/webview/new-session-view.ts, src/chat/sessions-tree.ts, src/chat/session-groups.ts, src/chat/webview/plan-step.ts, src/chat/chat-view-provider.ts, test/doc-migration.test.ts, test/mode-setup.test.ts, test/new-session-view.test.ts, test/model-settings.test.ts)
- Pruning what a spec already says [tested]: docMigrationPrompt (src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts) now states the Pruning stage's seven rules as bold lead-ins ("Covered section." … "Nothing covered."), between the in-scope-section rule and the confirmed-writes rule. docMigrationScope's readable/writable now include UNFILED_FILE ('plan/unfiled-decisions.md', from ./unfiled-decisions), so a contradiction ruling is written straight through, no permission prompt, the same way blind-plan and file-decisions record it — only docs/** cuts still go through the askable permission prompt. Also fixed the finding: blind-plan.ts's docsReviewPrompt and docsCutPrompt no longer bucket "covered or contradicts" as one list that "can go"; a covered section is offered for removal, a contradicting one is only reported ("which side is current is the user's to say") and, when the user rules the doc is current, recorded as an unfiled decision naming the feature via Edit on UNFILED_FILE (UNFILED_DECISIONS text), leaving the spec untouched. A later task building the Migrating/Verifying stages extends docMigrationPrompt after the "Nothing covered" line and docMigrationScope's writable (e.g. adding plan/*.spec.md) rather than re-deriving this. (files: src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts, src/agent/phases/blind-plan.ts, test/doc-migration.test.ts, test/reconcile.test.ts)
- Migrating the remaining feature docs into specs [tested]: docMigrationPrompt (src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts) now states the Migrating stage's six rules as bold lead-ins ("Offered when pruning is settled." … "Reviewed as any draft."), right after the Pruning stage's confirmed-doc-writes paragraph. docMigrationScope's writable now also includes SPECS_GLOB ('plan/*.spec.md', already imported from blind-plan.ts alongside the new PLAN_DIR import), so a migrated draft is written straight through like UNFILED_FILE, no permission prompt — only docs/** cuts still go through one. mode-setup.ts's 'doc-migration' case now composes new SpecContract(workspaceRoot) alongside its ScopeGuard, the same way 'plan' does, so a Write/Edit to plan/*.spec.md is checked against the spec contract and off-contract problems ride back on the tool result for the model to fix in the same turn. The "Built or planned" mark is carried as a `built: true`/`built: false` front-matter line on the draft itself, written by the model as part of the file it composes (no parsing code added — nothing reads it yet; a later task building the Verifying stage, which needs to tell a built feature's clean check from a planned one, reads it from there rather than inventing a new place to keep it). A later task extending the Verifying stage reads that front-matter field and the drafts this stage writes, rather than re-deriving where the mark lives. (files: src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts, src/agent/session/mode-setup.ts, test/doc-migration.test.ts, test/mode-setup.test.ts)
- Verifying a migrated feature against the code [tested]: SpecState (spec-file.ts) now carries `built: boolean`, read from the front-matter `built:` line by new `builtOf(text)`, alongside the existing `status`/`body`. deriveBoard (tasks-file.ts) takes two new optional params, `built = false` and `decisions: Decision[] = []`; a brand-new task for a scenario whose delivered rules none of the (non-withdrawn) decisions name gets `how` set to the new exported `TESTS_ONLY_HOW` constant, which `detail(task)` (task-board.ts, unchanged) already surfaces to the implementer verbatim. reconcilePrompt (reconcile.ts) gained a paragraph telling the check, for a spec whose front matter marks `built: true`, to ask whether the code already does each rule and to report an unsatisfied one as an ordinary decision rather than build it. chat-view-provider.ts's buildFromSpec now reads the decisions file and passes `spec.built` and the decisions through to deriveBoard, so production wiring matches the tested function. A later task needing "is this spec migrated built behaviour" reads `SpecState.built`; one needing "does this scenario still disagree" reads a task's `how === TESTS_ONLY_HOW` or re-derives from decisions' `on` lists, rather than inventing a new marker. (files: src/agent/phases/spec-file.ts, src/agent/phases/reconcile.ts, src/agent/phases/tasks-file.ts, src/chat/chat-view-provider.ts, test/spec-file.test.ts, test/tasks-file.test.ts, test/reconcile.test.ts, test/implement.test.ts, test/plan-review.test.ts, test/plan-stage.test.ts)

event.text:
The sweep's failure was not a code fault: all 120 files died before collection with "Vitest failed to find the runner" / "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')" — the worker-startup starvation already documented in `vitest.config.mts`, here hitting every worker at once (4.6s, environment 99%, no test ran). I could not reproduce it: `npm test` ran green eight times in a row (117 passed | 3 skipped, 1542 tests), the ten test files the board's tasks name ran green on their own, `npm run typecheck` is clean, and the installed vitest (5.0.3) matches package.json and the lockfile, installed hours before the sweep. The only way I got failures was by deliberately running three suites concurrently, which produced a different symptom (5s test timeouts and EBUSY on temp dirs under contention) — consistent with the sweep having run against a loaded machine rather than against broken code.

I changed no files; speculative pool tuning was tried before and traded this flake for jsdom state leaking between files, per the config's own note. All four tasks are back at tested with their files, proves and notes intact.
